text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Leader of opposition Benazir Bhutto said that the recent escalation of violence was the result of alliance between the ruling party and Mohajir National Movement (MQM).
- The government has issued letter of support to eight companies for setting up hydel plants having total capacity of 263 MW.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif starts a two-day visit to Tehran.

- Punjab province finance minister has presented the provincial budget for 1997/98 (July-June) with a total outlay of 147.72 billion, proposing to levy a number of new taxes to mobilise additional 15 billion rupees on its annual development schemes during 1997/98, a decrease of about five percent compared to the current fiscal year.
- The North West Frontier Province budget for 1997/98 will be presented in the provincial assembly on Monday.
- Eight Moslem countries joined forces, creating an economic and trading cooperation body to be known as the Developing Eight (D-8) group.
- Pakistan and Turkey have agreed to expand their defence cooperation and indentified a number of areas of common interest.
- Sri Lanka denied Tamil rebel claims that Pakistan jointly planned a military offensive in the island's north and said the charge was aimed at diverting attention from huge rebel losses.
- Nawaz Sharif has said he was deeply concerned about the deployment of Prithvi missiles by India along the border with Pakistan.
- The Balochistan provincial cabinet has approved the next financial year's budget proposals and the proposed annual development programme for 1997/98.
- Sindh Chief Minister Liaquat Jatoi, who also holds the portfolio of Financee, will present the 1997/98 budget before the Sindh provincial Assembly today.
- The earning per share of Pakistan Telecommunication Company limited will improve to 23.76 percent in 1997/98 over the previous year, a research report said.
